confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion, including all prompt appendices, additional analyses, and supplementary references; independently extracted the PDF pages supporting the recorded numbers.
Source version is arXiv:2608.26152v2, 28 Aug 2026, and the title/authors match; the PDF has 77 pages with Supplementary Information beginning on p. 25 (PDF p. 1 masthead; pp. 25?77).
Four web-based human experiments recruited native English-speaking Prolific participants (PDF pp. 18?19, Human?AI Collaborative Experiments).

No randomized AI-assistance study is confirmed. Experiment 4 uses between-person AI prompt type, within-person partner type, and counterbalanced order/category; neither AI-prompt allocation nor condition order is explicitly called randomized. Retain other/not_stated and eligibility criterion 1 unclear; false in this checker means randomization was not documented, not that non-random assignment was proven (PDF pp. 29?30, Experiment 4; full-text allocation search).
Explicit random assignment in Experiments 2 and 3 concerns the human sequence to be predicted, not receipt of AI assistance (PDF p. 29, Experiments 2?3).

Experiment 1 reports 36 completers, three categories, and three minutes per category; the timing pilot separately reports 36 human participants. Both reported human samples are below 50 and neither is an AI-assistance experiment (PDF p. 28, Experiment 1; p. 72, Figure S13A).

Experiment 2 reports 174 human predictors, 58 per category. Experiment 3 reports 181 prediction sessions (62 animals, 59 clothes, 60 supermarket items), separately identifying 92 participants contributing solo sequences; the pooled 190 valid solo sequences are not a people count (PDF pp. 18?19 and 29).

Experiment 4 reports an initial pool of 207, 192 people in 96 valid human?human dyads, and 144 valid human?AI sequences; 129 people have valid data in both conditions. These overlapping conditions must not be summed as independent people, and no separately stated randomized total is supplied (PDF pp. 11 and 29?30).

Full human?AI samples are 48 convergent, 46 divergent, and 50 inferred dyads, each with one human. Paired analyses instead use 45 convergent, 36 divergent, and 48 inferred participants, totaling the explicitly reported 129; the study exceeds 50 people despite smaller individual prompt arms (PDF p. 11; p. 71, Figure S12).

S2-O1 reported values exactly match: AI M = 0.138, 95% CI [0.128, 0.149]; human M = 0.079, 95% CI [0.071, 0.088]; +5.91 percentage points; W = 936.5, p < 0.0001, n = 174 (PDF p. 8, Cognitive Micro-Alignment).

S4-O1 and the one-line finding reproduce the reported individual-human fluency comparison, U = 1.45 ? 10^4, p = 0.44. Figure 5D labels the outcome as concepts produced by the individual human partner; the result is a non-significant difference (PDF p. 14, Figure 5D).

S4-O2 reported values exactly match: human?AI ?0.067 ? 0.008 SEM versus human?human ?0.044 ? 0.008 SEM; U = 1.57 ? 10^4, p = 3.63 ? 10^-2 uncorrected, p_corrected = 7.27 ? 10^-2. The comparison is not significant after Holm?Bonferroni correction and concerns within-person self-similarity, not across-person homogenization (PDF p. 74, Figure S15A).

The archival counts are 141 human-generated animal sequences and 699 human trajectories, with 648 complete sequences in paired context-control analyses; these are correctly distinguished from a confirmed new participant count (PDF pp. 6 and 10).

The model-only temporal probe uses 50 human sequences as contexts; the simulated dyads use starting words from 699 human sequences. Neither constitutes randomized human receipt of AI help (PDF p. 64, Figure S6; p. 67, Figure S8).

Gemini-3-Pro supplies the main independent prediction results; collaborative partners use Llama-3.3 70B-Instruct with divergent, convergent, or inferred prompts and calibrated response delays (PDF pp. 8, 11, 17, and 30?31).

The source is an original multi-experiment paper, not a synthesis; null synthesis counts and absent pooled meta-analytic estimates are appropriate (PDF pp. 18?19 and 28?31). The included supplement contains regression standard errors and paired counts/tests (PDF p. 66, Table S3; p. 71, Figure S12).
summary: The source version and reported statistics match the PDF, but context coding, outcome coverage, exclusions, and provenance need correction. Random assignment of AI assistance is not documented; the collaboration experiment reports counterbalancing and 129 participants in paired analyses.
